text:
maya: Heads-up — our hosted GPU consumption for rtx-series in us-west-2 spiked last week; committed hours vs usage: looks like a gap. Can we run a quick sanity check on commitments and possible double-billing?

alex: Noted. I saw the same in the daily cost dashboard. 24h peak was ~2200 GPU-hrs, commitments show 1600. :thinking_face:

samir: Is that normalized to T4-equivalent or raw GPU count? Our contracts are billed per vGPU-hour (p4-equivalent) so mismatch can be unit conversion.

alex: Dashboard is raw GPU-hrs across instance families. I'll pull a conversion table.

maya: Also check if Hosted burst nodes (ephemeral) were misattributed to the committed pool due to the tagging bug from last deploy.

chris: Which deploy? The autoscaler change on Tue? I added a tag patch but might have missed a path.

alex: Found a strange thing in billing export: two line items for 'us-west-2/gpu:shared' and 'us-west-2/gpu:dedicated' for the same timeframe. Could be billing overlap when we hit burst cap.

billing-bot: [automated] New billing export CSV available: s3://redwood-invoice-staging/bill-2026-03-10.csv

samir: I ran a quick calc converting to p4e equivalents: peak 2200 raw -> ~1800 p4e-hrs. So still ~200hr gap vs commitments.

maya: OK so part conversion, part actual over-usage. Action items:
- alex: crosswalk billing line items -> tag owner
- chris: verify autoscaler tag paths + deploy diff
- samir: recompute commitments vs p4e normalized forecast for last 90 days and next 30 days

alex: I can start on crosswalk. Quick SQL I'll run:
```
SELECT bill_item, sum(gpu_hours) FROM billing_export
WHERE region='us-west-2' AND date>='2026-02-01'
GROUP BY bill_item;
```

chris: I'll scan deploys from Tue-Fri and push a hotfix if tag mismatch found. If autoscaler falls back to shared pool, we should throttle burst earlier.

maya: Also check whether customer A's high-throughput tests were run in prod by mistake — that happened before.

alex: FYI, cost alerts triggered at 18:12 on 2026-03-09 — alert channel shows "backfill jobs" by service:ingest. Was that scheduled?

samir: Not scheduled. Looking at job history now.

billing-bot: [automated] Alert: Cost anomaly detected us-west-2 GPU spend +36% vs 7d avg.

chris: If we confirm it's an incident, we should file a short postmortem and consider buying a small top-up commitment to avoid overnight overrun while we mitigate.

maya: Good point — can we get procurement to approve a 90-day cushion with quick commit? That buys time and reduces overage rate.

alex: I'll annotate the billing export with line-level tags and link PR to this thread.

samir: I'll update the forecast sheet and include two scenarios: (1) immediate tag fix -> consumption returns normal, (2) no fix -> we need +25% commitment in us-west-2.

maya: Thanks. Ping me when you have the annotated export. Also add a column with `p4e_equivalent_hours` so finance can see unit economics.

alex: Will do. ETA 2h.

samir: ETA for forecast update: 4h.

chris: Hotfix deploy if tag gap found: 1h after confirmation.

maya: Great. Let's reconvene here once we have numbers. :thumbsup:
